meta.label: Books & reading
meta.attribution: Curated from public ownership, library, DRM/licensing, labor/competition and bookstore-support sources - not audited data. The same book is often identical everywhere; the choice is who you support and what you can truly own. Every criterion has a cited basis; reviewed 2026-06. Suggest changes via Contribute.

reads.text: Compare books & reading by labor and sourcing, price, local support, and openness.

axes.label: Cost or overall fit
axes.question: Lower cost or a stronger overall fit?

consumer.axes: Round 8 practical decision dials, with the S4 cost-or-values default where evidence permits.
consumer.budget: Round 8 honest budget eligibility, with S4 refusing to guess missing cost data.
consumer.archetypes: Round 8 computed answer slots matched to available category evidence.
consumer.page: Round 7 personal precedence extended in Round 9 to the shared decision page for every live category.

products.name: Your public library
products.description: A local public institution for borrowing print and digital books, often the strongest default when access and community matter.

ethics.note: Public libraries serve readers without a profit motive and are anchored in community access, though digital licensing can strain budgets.

local.note: a local public institution

openness.note: Print borrowing is open and durable, while library ebooks are usually licensed/DRM-controlled rather than owned by patrons.

selection.note: WorldCat is the world's largest library catalog and helps find library materials near you.

price.note: free

products.name: Libby / OverDrive
products.description: A library-card app for borrowing ebooks, audiobooks, and magazines from participating public libraries.

ethics.note: Public-library access model, with ALA pressure for more flexible and cost-effective digital-content licensing.

local.note: Access runs through a participating library card rather than a retail account alone.

openness.note: Library Futures' ownership principles explain that licensed ebooks can restrict library preservation, sharing and patron privacy compared with owned print collections.

selection.note: OverDrive says library-selected ebooks and audiobooks are available through Libby; catalog varies by library.

price.note: Free to patrons through participating libraries.

products.name: Hoopla Digital
products.description: A library-funded media app with instant borrowing for many ebooks, audiobooks, comics, music, and video titles.

ethics.note: Expands free patron access, but BPL discontinued Hoopla after September 2025, citing an unsustainable pay-per-use model and costs above other digital resources.

local.note: Hoopla access is provided through local public libraries and requires a library card.

openness.note: Licensed access only: Hoopla terms allow in-app streaming/downloads but not extracting, copying, or owning files.

selection.note: Broad media catalog including ebooks, audiobooks, comics, music, movies, and TV; titles vary by library.

price.note: Free to patrons where their public library pays for access.

products.name: Local independent bookshop
products.description: A nearby independent seller that keeps more of the book spend in local bookselling instead of a dominant platform channel.

ethics.note: IndieBound describes local-first independent bookstores as keeping payroll, taxes and purchases in the community.

local.note: the most local option there is

openness.note: print you fully own, DRM-free

selection.note: Independent shops are curated and can often order books, but they do not match a platform monopoly's instant catalog.

price.note: list price; no monopoly discounts

products.name: Powell's Books
products.description: A large independent new-and-used bookstore with online ordering and a real physical bookselling culture.

ethics.note: Powell's is a large independent bookstore rather than a platform monopoly.

local.note: Portland-based independent store with physical shops

openness.note: print books you own outright

selection.note: claims world's largest independent bookstore; broad new, used, and rare selection

price.note: used books and promos help, but not built around monopoly discounting

products.name: Hive.co.uk
products.description: A UK online bookshop where each purchase supports a chosen independent high-street bookshop.

ethics.note: Hive says every purchase supports a chosen independent UK bookshop through commission.

local.note: customer chooses a UK bookshop to receive commission

openness.note: print books are owned; ebook DRM varies by publisher

selection.note: broad UK online books and ebook catalog

price.note: Hive discounts exist, but the model prioritizes shop commission over always-lowest price.

products.name: Project Gutenberg / Standard Ebooks
products.description: A free public-domain ebook path for classics and older works, strongest when you want DRM-free files you keep.

ethics.note: Project Gutenberg is a volunteer-created public-domain ebook commons.

local.note: nonprofit/volunteer

openness.note: free, DRM-free, public-domain files you own forever

selection.note: Project Gutenberg focuses on older public-domain works, so current bestsellers are intentionally absent.

price.note: free

products.name: LibriVox
products.description: A volunteer-run commons for free public-domain audiobooks read by people around the world.

ethics.note: Non-commercial, non-profit, ad-free, volunteer-powered public-domain audiobook project.

local.note: Global volunteer commons rather than a local bookseller or local library institution.

openness.note: LibriVox donates recordings to the public domain for free reuse.

selection.note: Limited to public-domain texts chosen by volunteers, so it is excellent for classics but not new releases.

price.note: Audiobooks are free to listen to and download.

products.name: Open Library / Internet Archive
products.description: A nonprofit, editable catalog and digital lending library that expands access while carrying real publisher-rights controversy.

ethics.note: Internet Archive expanded digital access, but the 2024 Hachette endpoint still means it honors AAP member publisher requests to remove books from lending.

local.note: library-commons model rather than a local shop

openness.note: Open Library loans expire, are restricted by lending rules, and may be removed for publisher-rights reasons; access is not DRM-free ownership.

selection.note: Open Library remains a broad catalog with free read-or-borrow access where available, but loans are item-by-item, time-limited and availability-constrained.

price.note: free to read or borrow where available

products.name: OpenStax
products.description: A nonprofit Rice University project publishing free, peer-reviewed, openly licensed textbooks for high school and college.

ethics.note: OpenStax is a Rice University nonprofit whose materials have reached 43.4 million learners and saved students $3.4 billion.

local.note: Nonprofit educational commons rather than a local bookstore or local library channel.

openness.note: OpenStax textbooks are free, peer-reviewed, and openly licensed for use and adaptation.

selection.note: Strong for standard K12 and higher-ed subjects, but intentionally limited compared with a general bookstore catalog.

price.note: Digital textbooks are free online, with low-cost print options for readers who want paper.

products.name: Bookshare
products.description: A nonprofit accessible-ebook library for readers with qualifying print disabilities, strongest when format access is the barrier.

ethics.note: Bookshare is a Benetech 501(c)(3) nonprofit initiative for readers who need accessible formats.

local.note: Nonprofit access library rather than a local bookstore; value is strongest for eligible readers and schools.

openness.note: Books are available in accessible formats such as EPUB, DAISY, BRF, and MP3, but membership requires qualifying eligibility.

selection.note: Bookshare says members can access over 1.4 million titles in more than 40 languages.

price.note: Free for qualified US students and schools; US non-student individual membership is $79.99 per year.

products.name: Leanpub
products.description: An author-direct ebook platform, especially strong for technical books, with high author royalties and no DRM.

ethics.note: Leanpub says authors earn 80% royalties on purchases of $7.99 and up.

local.note: online author-direct platform, not a local bookshop

openness.note: Leanpub states ebooks have no DRM

selection.note: strong niche catalog, especially programming and professional topics

price.note: variable pricing and memberships; not always the cheapest route

products.name: StoryBundle
products.description: A time-limited pay-what-you-want bundle site for indie ebooks, with DRM-free files and author/charity split controls.

ethics.note: Built around indie-author bundles; live bundle pages disclose author/StoryBundle splits and optional charity donation.

local.note: Author-supportive online marketplace, but not a local bookstore or library institution.

openness.note: Author FAQ describes bundles as DRM-free .mobi and .epub files readable across devices.

selection.note: Bundles are curated, time-limited sets rather than an always-on full bookstore catalog.

price.note: Pay-what-you-want bundle pricing, often with higher tiers for bonus books.

products.name: Smashwords Store
products.description: A long-running indie ebook storefront, now part of Draft2Digital, with DRM-free downloads and author-set ebook pricing.

ethics.note: Draft2Digital lists Smashwords Store royalties at 75% for ebooks priced $2.99 or higher, or 40% below $2.99.

local.note: Global author marketplace rather than a local bookstore or public library channel.

openness.note: Draft2Digital's Smashwords FAQ says books uploaded to Smashwords do not contain DRM technology.

selection.note: Draft2Digital's acquisition announcement described 800,000+ titles from 250,000 authors and publishers across the combined platform.

price.note: Authors can set ebook prices and use Smashwords-specific coupons or free pricing, but catalog prices vary by title.

products.name: Bookshop.org
products.description: An online bookstore whose model routes margin to independent bookshops rather than a dominant retail platform.

ethics.note: Bookshop.org is a certified B Corp whose mission is helping local independent bookstores thrive.

local.note: Bookshop.org gives 10% of regular sales to a shared bookstore pool and 30% of cover price to affiliate stores on linked sales.

openness.note: Print books are owned outright, while Bookshop.org ebooks are read through its apps rather than offered as a DRM-free file-first model.

selection.note: broad online catalog

price.note: Not usually the lowest-price channel; the model intentionally routes margin to independent bookstores.

products.name: Bookshop.org ebooks
products.description: An ebook storefront that lets digital purchases support independent bookstores, with app/browser reading and limited DRM-free transfer.

ethics.note: Bookshop.org positions its ebook store around buying ebooks while financially supporting local independent bookstores.

local.note: Ebook purchases can support local independent bookstores through Bookshop.org's bookstore-support model.

openness.note: Most Bookshop.org ebooks must be read in its Apple/Android apps or web browser; only DRM-free titles can be downloaded and transferred.

selection.note: The mobile app listing describes a store of millions of ebooks, but Kindle/Kobo/Nook compatibility depends on DRM-free status.

price.note: Regular ebook retail pricing, with the value tradeoff being bookstore support rather than always-lowest price.

products.name: Libro.fm
products.description: An audiobook store and subscription service that lets purchases support a chosen local bookstore.

ethics.note: Libro.fm says every purchase supports a chosen local bookshop, shares purchase profits with that shop, and is a Certified B Corporation.

local.note: Libro.fm says its community includes 20,000+ booksellers from 4,000+ bookshops and supports bookshops internationally.

openness.note: Libro.fm support says every audiobook is DRM-free and can be downloaded as MP3 or M4B files.

selection.note: Broad audiobook catalog, but some titles cannot be bought with membership credits because of publisher restrictions.

price.note: Membership and a la carte purchases are available, with publisher restrictions on a minority of credit redemptions.

products.name: Secondhand / used (ThriftBooks, charity shops)
products.description: A circular route for cheap print books, especially strong when used copies or charity shops fit the need.

ethics.note: Used books reduce new production; large online used sellers are circular but not the same as local charity shops.

local.note: local charity shops keep value local

openness.note: print you own

selection.note: vast but luck-of-the-draw

price.note: cheap

products.name: Better World Books
products.description: A mission-driven used-book retailer that pairs circular bookselling with library and literacy support.

ethics.note: B Lab says Better World Books has raised millions for libraries/literacy and reused or recycled hundreds of millions of books.

local.note: online, but mission-driven

openness.note: print you own

selection.note: large used catalog

price.note: affordable; free shipping

products.name: World of Books
products.description: A large used-book reseller built around keeping books in circulation, strongest for affordable secondhand print.

ethics.note: B Lab lists World of Books Group as a Certified B Corporation focused on used books, reuse, charities, and circular economy.

local.note: World of Books buys significant surplus volumes from UK and Ireland charity shops, but remains an online reseller rather than a local shop.

openness.note: Used print books are owned outright and can be kept, lent, resold, or donated.

selection.note: B Lab describes World of Books Group as a leading global seller of used books online.

price.note: Secondhand resale can be inexpensive, though availability and condition vary by title.

products.name: Biblio
products.description: An independent marketplace for used, rare, and collectible books from independent booksellers around the world.

ethics.note: Biblio describes itself as the largest independent book marketplace and says it works with independent booksellers.

local.note: Marketplace purchases support independent sellers, though the transaction is still mediated by an online platform.

openness.note: Used print books are owned outright and can be kept, lent, resold, or donated.

selection.note: Biblio says it offers over 100 million used and rare books.

price.note: Used-book pricing can be affordable, with visible low-price listings and frequent-reader discounts, but collectible titles vary widely.

products.name: Alibris
products.description: A marketplace for new, used, rare, and out-of-print books from thousands of independent sellers.

ethics.note: Alibris says it connects buyers to more than 200 million items from thousands of independent sellers worldwide.

local.note: Supports independent sellers through a marketplace model, but is not the same as buying directly from a local bookshop.

openness.note: Used and new print books are owned outright; Alibris also operates in ebooks, where openness depends on format and publisher terms.

selection.note: Alibris describes a marketplace of more than 200 million books, music, and movie items.

price.note: Used-book marketplace pricing can be low and competitive, though shipping, seller, and condition vary.

products.name: AbeBooks
products.description: A large used, rare, and collectible book marketplace with many independent sellers, owned by Amazon since 2008.

ethics.note: AbeBooks connects independent sellers, but its own about page says it is a subsidiary of Amazon.com, Inc.

local.note: The marketplace supports professional booksellers worldwide, but Amazon ownership weakens the local-independent fit.

openness.note: Used print books are owned outright, even when the marketplace layer is centralized.

selection.note: AbeBooks describes millions of used books across genres, languages, out-of-print editions, and collectible categories.

price.note: AbeBooks advertises millions of cheap used books, including under-$10 selections and seller-dependent shipping.

products.name: Barnes & Noble / NOOK
products.description: A major U.S. bookstore chain and NOOK ebook platform, stronger for physical-store access than for digital ownership.

ethics.note: Barnes & Noble operates hundreds of U.S. bookstores and a NOOK digital business, but it is still a large corporate chain rather than an indie channel.

local.note: Physical bookstores create local access and events, but ownership and purchasing power remain centralized.

openness.note: NOOK terms grant a limited license and require maintaining DRM for digital content transfers.

selection.note: Barnes & Noble sells print books, NOOK ebooks, audiobooks, magazines, and broad subject categories online and in stores.

price.note: Offers mainstream retail pricing plus member rewards and ebook deals, but not the consistently lowest used-book path.

products.name: Kobo (Rakuten)
products.description: A mainstream ebook and e-reader platform that is more interoperable than Kindle in some workflows, but still DRM-limited.

ethics.note: a real Amazon alternative; supports library lending (OverDrive)

local.note: global retailer

openness.note: Kobo supports EPUB/Adobe DRM workflows, which are more interoperable than Kindle but still often DRM-limited.

selection.note: large e-book catalog

price.note: comparable to Kindle

products.name: Google Play Books
products.description: A large mainstream ebook and audiobook store with offline reading and some exportability, but still a Google account platform.

ethics.note: Large corporate platform; less bookstore-supportive than indie or library options, but open to publisher/author partners in supported countries.

local.note: Global Google retail platform, not a local bookstore or library channel.

openness.note: Some purchased ebooks can be exported as EPUB/PDF, but publisher export limits, rentals, and Adobe DRM remain constraints.

selection.note: Google Play listing describes millions of ebooks, audiobooks, comics, and manga.

price.note: A la carte purchases with no subscription requirement; pricing varies by title and country.

products.name: Apple Books
products.description: A polished mainstream ebook and audiobook store tied to Apple's account and device ecosystem.

ethics.note: mainstream platform

local.note: global

openness.note: Apple Books supports publisher DRM settings, so many purchased ebooks are tied to Apple's reading ecosystem.

selection.note: large

price.note: list-ish

products.name: Everand
products.description: A Scribd-family subscription for ebooks and audiobooks: broad and affordable for heavy readers, but access lasts only while subscribed.

ethics.note: Everand expands paid access to a large reading library, but it is a centralized subscription platform rather than an indie bookstore or library commons.

local.note: Global subscription platform with no local bookstore or library-support mechanism.

openness.note: The subscriber agreement says access is to Everand's digital library during the subscription period, so it is not ownership of portable files.

selection.note: Everand advertises access to 1.5M+ books plus unlimited access to thousands of additional books, audiobooks, and podcasts.

price.note: Subscription pricing can be good value for heavy readers, but availability and unlock limits are platform-controlled.

products.name: Storytel
products.description: A large international audiobook and ebook subscription, especially relevant outside the U.S., with access tied to the plan.

ethics.note: Subscription model gives readers access without Amazon ownership, but it remains a centralized platform rather than a local or open commons.

local.note: Storytel is an international streaming service, not a local bookstore or library-support model.

openness.note: Storytel terms describe consumption limits by plan and renewal by billing period, which indicates access rather than portable ownership.

selection.note: Storytel advertises 800,000+ stories in 40 languages.

price.note: Monthly plans can be economical for frequent listeners, but plan hours and carry-over rules vary by market.

products.name: Audiobooks.com
products.description: A mainstream audiobook subscription and purchase platform with a large catalog, but little local or open-ownership advantage.

ethics.note: Mainstream commercial audiobook platform with recurring membership; no indie-bookshop support or broad values certification found.

local.note: Global subscription retailer rather than a local bookstore, library, or cooperative channel.

openness.note: Terms center on account membership and subscription access, so it is less open than DRM-free download sellers.

selection.note: Audiobooks.com advertises 700,000+ premium titles.

price.note: Monthly credit pricing is convenient but can leave light listeners paying for a recurring plan.

products.name: Kobo Plus
products.description: Kobo's monthly read/listen subscription is a useful Kindle Unlimited alternative, but still subscription access rather than ownership.

ethics.note: Kobo Plus is a real non-Amazon subscription alternative, but it is still a corporate platform rather than an indie or library channel.

local.note: Rakuten Kobo platform access, not local bookstore support.

openness.note: Kobo Plus is monthly access to read and listen, not permanent DRM-free file ownership.

selection.note: Kobo Plus provides unlimited reading/listening from the Kobo Plus catalog; available titles vary by country.

price.note: Fixed monthly price can be good for heavy readers/listeners, with plans varying by market.

products.name: Downpour
products.description: An audiobook store and membership option notable because much of its catalog is DRM-free, though publisher restrictions still apply.

ethics.note: Commercial audiobook retailer, but stronger user-control signal than locked subscription platforms because much content is DRM-free.

local.note: Online audiobook retailer with no local bookstore-support mechanism.

openness.note: Downpour FAQ says much of its content is DRM-free, while some publisher-required titles remain DRM-protected.

selection.note: Useful audiobook catalog, but smaller and more variable than Amazon/Audible-scale platforms.

price.note: Offers a membership/rental/purchase model, so value depends on listening frequency and title availability.

products.name: Chirp
products.description: A no-subscription audiobook deals store: strong for bargain hunters, less open than DRM-free download shops.

ethics.note: Chirp avoids recurring subscription/credit pressure; purchases are a la carte rather than a lock-in membership.

local.note: Discount audiobook retailer with no library or local bookstore-support mechanism.

openness.note: Chirp says purchased audiobooks are yours to keep, but listening is centered on the Chirp app rather than DRM-free file downloads.

selection.note: Deal catalog is useful but deal-driven and narrower than full-catalog audiobook stores.

price.note: Chirp advertises limited-time audiobook deals up to 95% off with no subscription fees.

products.name: Audible (Amazon)
products.description: Amazon's dominant audiobook subscription platform, strong on catalog and convenience but weak on ownership and independence.

ethics.note: Audible is Amazon-owned; Amazon faces FTC monopoly allegations and worker-safety scrutiny elsewhere in the business.

local.note: Amazon-owned global platform rather than a local bookstore or library channel.

openness.note: Audible emphasizes app/offline listening and subscription access, but it does not offer Libro.fm-style DRM-free file ownership.

selection.note: Audible has a very large audiobook and originals catalog with bestsellers, new releases, exclusives, and genre shelves.

price.note: Membership pricing uses credits and included-title access; Premium credits can buy a title kept after cancellation.

products.name: Amazon / Kindle
products.description: The dominant ebook retail platform: huge selection and discounts, with Amazon lock-in and license-style ownership tradeoffs.

ethics.note: FTC alleges Amazon maintains monopoly power through anticompetitive strategies; Amazon disputes the allegations.

local.note: Kindle/Amazon is a global platform channel, not a local bookstore or library institution.

openness.note: Amazon's Kindle terms define Kindle books as digital content licenses, not unrestricted ownership.

selection.note: Amazon's Kindle ecosystem has a very large catalog; Kindle Unlimited alone advertises access to more than 5 million digital titles.

price.note: Often price-competitive through discounts and subscriptions, but the low-friction price comes with Kindle ecosystem lock-in.

products.name: ThriftBooks
products.description: A large used-book retailer: strong on price, selection and recirculation, weaker on local-bookshop support.

ethics.note: ThriftBooks sells used books and promotes buyback/recirculation, a useful circular-economy signal even though it is a large centralized retailer.

local.note: ThriftBooks is a national online used-book retailer rather than a local bookshop, though its model can recirculate library and household books.

openness.note: Used print books are owned physical goods with no DRM, account lock-in, or licensing wrapper.

selection.note: ThriftBooks says it has more than 13 million titles available, including used, out-of-print and rare books.

price.note: ThriftBooks positions itself around cheap used books and free standard US shipping above its threshold.

products.name: PangoBooks
products.description: A reader-to-reader used-book marketplace that keeps books moving, with more platform convenience than local-bookshop character.

ethics.note: PangoBooks is a marketplace where readers sell directly from their collections to other readers, extending the life of existing books.

local.note: The direct-reader marketplace is more person-to-person than Amazon-style retail, but it is not the same as buying from a local bookshop.

openness.note: PangoBooks transactions are for used physical books, so readers own the copy rather than renting a licensed ebook.

selection.note: PangoBooks says readers can buy and sell used books across ordinary books, special editions, children's books and textbooks.

price.note: PangoBooks emphasizes deals and savings on used books, with pricing set by individual sellers.

products.name: Oxfam second-hand books
products.description: A charity-led second-hand book route, especially strong in the UK, where the purchase also supports Oxfam's wider mission.

ethics.note: Oxfam sells donated second-hand books online and through shops, turning used books into charity revenue.

local.note: Oxfam runs physical charity shops and bookshops, so it can support a local high-street reuse channel in places where shops exist.

openness.note: Second-hand print books are owned physical goods, with no ebook platform lock-in.

selection.note: Oxfam's online shop lists thousands of second-hand books, but inventory depends on donations and is less predictable than giant retail catalogs.

price.note: Used-book charity retail is generally affordable, though collectible or unusual books may be priced differently.

products.name: No Starch Press
products.description: A specialist technical publisher that is unusually strong for DRM-free ebook ownership, but narrow in subject coverage.

ethics.note: Buying direct from an independent technical publisher can support the publisher/author channel more directly than a dominant marketplace.

local.note: No Starch is a direct publisher channel rather than a local bookstore or library route.

openness.note: No Starch says most titles are available as DRM-free ebook bundles containing PDF, Mobi and EPUB files.

selection.note: The catalog is strong for programming, security, Linux and maker topics but intentionally narrower than general book retailers.

price.note: No Starch often includes a free ebook edition with print purchases from its site, but individual technical books can still cost more than used copies.

products.name: O'Reilly Learning
products.description: A deep professional learning library with huge technical selection, but subscription pricing and platform access rather than ownership.

ethics.note: O'Reilly is a professional learning platform and publisher; it is useful for skill-building but not a local or author-direct book channel.

local.note: O'Reilly Learning is a global subscription platform, not a local bookstore or library institution.

openness.note: The core offering is platform/app access to a subscription library, not DRM-free files the reader owns outright.

selection.note: O'Reilly advertises 60K+ titles plus video, live online courses, case studies and playlists.

price.note: O'Reilly's individual plan is listed at $49/month or $499/year, which is expensive unless the catalog replaces many separate purchases.

products.name: Humble book bundles
products.description: A rotating bundle option that can be excellent value for DRM-free ebooks and charity splits, but catalog fit depends on the current bundle.

ethics.note: Humble book bundles have historically let buyers allocate portions to authors, charities and Humble, though bundle terms vary.

local.note: Humble is a global online bundle marketplace rather than a local bookstore channel.

openness.note: Humble ebook bundles are often distributed as downloadable DRM-free files, commonly including formats such as PDF, EPUB and MOBI.

selection.note: Selection is strong only when a relevant limited-time bundle is live; it is not a stable all-books catalog.

price.note: Bundle pricing can be extremely low per title compared with buying books individually.

products.name: HathiTrust Digital Library
products.description: A massive research-library digital collection, strongest for scholarly discovery and public-domain reading rather than current commercial books.

ethics.note: HathiTrust is built around stewarding digitized knowledge through research libraries rather than retailing books.

local.note: Its value comes from member libraries preserving and opening collections, though it is not a neighborhood bookstore channel.

openness.note: Anyone can search without an account and HathiTrust says up to 40% of the collection is available for anyone to read online.

selection.note: HathiTrust describes an 18-million-plus item digitized collection, especially useful for older and scholarly material.

price.note: Public full-view items are free to read online; some access depends on rights status or institutional membership.

products.name: Digital Public Library of America
products.description: A free discovery portal for texts, images, video, and sound from libraries, archives, museums, and cultural institutions.

ethics.note: DPLA is structured around public access to cultural collections rather than book retail.

local.note: DPLA brings together materials from libraries, archives and museums, making institutional collections easier to discover.

openness.note: DPLA makes collections freely available online, but rights and reuse vary by item and holding institution.

selection.note: DPLA lists more than 53 million images, texts, videos and sounds, though it is broader than a bookstore catalog.

price.note: The discovery portal is free to use, with many public digital materials available without payment.

products.name: Directory of Open Access Books
products.description: A free directory for finding peer-reviewed open-access academic books from many scholarly publishers.

ethics.note: DOAB is a community-driven discovery service for peer-reviewed open-access books, not a paywalled retailer.

local.note: It supports scholarly open infrastructure, but it is not a local bookstore or public-library lending channel.

openness.note: DOAB says all services are free of charge and all data is freely available.

selection.note: DOAB lists more than 107,000 peer-reviewed books, with strength in academic and scholarly material.

price.note: The books indexed are open access, so the reader-facing discovery and access path is free where publisher links remain available.

products.name: OAPEN Library
products.description: An open-access repository for peer-reviewed academic books, especially useful for scholarly monographs and research collections.

ethics.note: OAPEN is a not-for-profit foundation dedicated to open-access books and library-supported infrastructure.

local.note: OAPEN is a global scholarly repository rather than a local retail or lending institution.

openness.note: The library surfaces open-access titles with visible Creative Commons licensing information across the collection.

selection.note: OAPEN shows tens of thousands of book and chapter records across publishers, languages, subjects and collections.

price.note: OAPEN's reader value is free access to open-access scholarly books rather than paid ebook checkout.

products.name: Open Textbook Library
products.description: A curated library of open textbooks that can reduce course-material costs when a suitable text exists for the class.

ethics.note: Open textbooks directly address textbook affordability and allow reuse and adaptation rather than one-time commercial access.

local.note: The library is institutionally hosted and education-focused, but adoption depends on instructors rather than a local shop.

openness.note: Open Textbook Library says books are licensed to be freely used and adapted, and can be downloaded, edited and distributed at no cost.

selection.note: The catalog lists 1,830 open textbooks, broad for education but narrow compared with general bookstores.

price.note: Books can be downloaded and used at no cost, making this one of the strongest textbook affordability options where coverage fits.

products.name: Pressbooks Directory
products.description: A searchable index of open-access books and educational resources created across Pressbooks networks.

ethics.note: Pressbooks supports open education and makes it easier to adapt, remix and publish learning materials.

local.note: The directory aggregates institution-published resources rather than supporting a local bookstore directly.

openness.note: Pressbooks describes the directory as a free searchable catalog of open-access books.

selection.note: Pressbooks Directory lists more than 9,000 open-access books, mostly educational and institutional materials.

price.note: Directory access is free and most value comes from freely available open educational resources.

products.name: JSTOR Open Access Books
products.description: A scholarly reading path for thousands of open-access ebooks on JSTOR, strongest for academic and humanities/social-science use.

ethics.note: JSTOR's open-access books program expands reader access while attempting to sustain scholarly publishers and presses.

local.note: JSTOR is a platform and library infrastructure service, not a local bookshop or neighborhood library branch.

openness.note: JSTOR says its open-and-free collection includes thousands of DRM-free open-access ebooks from scholarly publishers.

selection.note: JSTOR librarian guidance reports 9,000-plus open-access ebook titles, with emphasis on respected scholarly presses.

price.note: Open-access ebooks on JSTOR are available at no cost to users and libraries for those titles.

products.name: The Palace Project
products.description: A library-centered app that can bring multiple library ebook and audiobook sources into one place where participating libraries offer it.

ethics.note: Palace frames itself around putting libraries at the center of digital reading access.

local.note: Access runs through participating libraries and a patron's library relationship rather than a retail account alone.

openness.note: Strong library access, but most current ebooks and audiobooks remain borrowed platform content rather than reader-owned DRM-free files.

selection.note: The Palace marketplace advertises more than 1.2M ebooks and audiobooks plus open-access and simultaneous-use titles.

price.note: For patrons, Palace is used through library access rather than per-title retail payment.

products.name: cloudLibrary
products.description: A library digital-content app for borrowing ebooks and audiobooks where a public library subscribes to the platform.

ethics.note: cloudLibrary expands free patron access through libraries, though it is still vendor-run digital lending infrastructure.

local.note: Readers access cloudLibrary through their own participating library rather than a general retail account.

openness.note: The model is borrowing from a library's digital collection, so access is convenient but not reader-owned or DRM-free.

selection.note: OCLC describes cloudLibrary as helping libraries provide ebooks, audiobooks, magazines, newspapers, comics, graphic novels, manga and streaming video.

price.note: Patrons browse, borrow and read through their library rather than buying each ebook or audiobook.

products.name: Sora by OverDrive Education
products.description: A student reading app for borrowing ebooks and audiobooks from a participating school's digital library.

ethics.note: Sora gives students school-managed access to ebooks and audiobooks selected for their community.

local.note: Students sign in through a school library or district, making the access route institution-based and local to education.

openness.note: Sora is a borrowing and streaming/downloading platform for school library collections, not a DRM-free ownership model.

selection.note: Catalog strength depends on the school's hand-selected collection; OverDrive reported 100M-plus digital books accessed through Sora.

price.note: Sora is free to students where their school provides access.

products.name: eBooks.com
products.description: A long-running ebook retailer with a large catalog and some DRM-free titles, but many books still use publisher DRM.

ethics.note: eBooks.com is an ebook retail channel selling publisher books worldwide, but it is not author-direct, local or library-based.

local.note: It is a global online ebook store rather than a local bookstore or library-supporting purchase path.

openness.note: eBooks.com sells both DRM-protected and DRM-free formats, so ownership portability depends heavily on the title.

selection.note: eBooks.com says it sells millions of ebooks from local and global publishers to a worldwide audience.

price.note: Pricing is conventional retail by title; there is no library-card or broad free-access model.

products.name: BookFinder.com
products.description: A price-comparison search tool for new, used, rare, out-of-print and textbook listings across many sellers.

ethics.note: BookFinder can route readers toward used and out-of-print books, but it is a comparison layer rather than a mission retailer.

local.note: It compares offers from many booksellers worldwide, which can include smaller sellers but does not specifically privilege local shops.

openness.note: Physical used and rare books are generally owned after purchase, unlike locked ebook platforms.

selection.note: BookFinder says it compares offers from more than 100,000 booksellers worldwide across new, used, rare, out-of-print and textbook books.

price.note: Price comparison across sellers can substantially reduce cost, especially for textbooks and used books.

products.name: WorldCat
products.description: A global library-catalog search route for finding books in nearby library collections before buying.

ethics.note: WorldCat is operated by OCLC as a library discovery network built from member-library collections, not as a retail bookstore.

local.note: WorldCat helps readers discover which libraries hold a title, making local borrowing and interlibrary discovery easier.

openness.note: It is a discovery layer rather than an ownership format; openness depends on the library item, license or lending model behind each result.

selection.note: OCLC describes WorldCat as a comprehensive database of library-collection information with books, videos, photos and other resources.

price.note: Searching is free and successful use often routes through library access, though borrowing rules vary by library.

products.name: LibraryThing
products.description: A long-running reader catalog and recommendation community for tracking personal libraries outside the Amazon-owned Goodreads default.

ethics.note: LibraryThing emphasizes cataloging and reader community rather than retail lock-in, with limited sign-up information required.

local.note: It can support small libraries and community catalogs through TinyCat, but it is not itself a local bookstore or public-library lender.

openness.note: LibraryThing draws catalog data from libraries and Amazon sources, and lets readers manage their own catalog, but it does not provide DRM-free books.

selection.note: The service says it uses the Library of Congress, multiple Amazon sites and more than 2,200 libraries worldwide for cataloging.

price.note: LibraryThing says individual and organizational users can catalog any number of books for free.

products.name: The StoryGraph
products.description: An Amazon-free Goodreads alternative focused on reading stats, mood-based discovery, content warnings and social reading tools.

ethics.note: The StoryGraph positions itself as an Amazon-free Goodreads alternative, which matters for readers avoiding Amazon-owned discovery defaults.

local.note: It is a digital catalog and recommendation service, not a local bookstore, library lender or indie-retail purchasing route.

openness.note: The service helps track owned books and reading lists, but it does not itself provide open or DRM-free book files.

selection.note: StoryGraph offers book search, tracking, tags, challenges, book clubs, content warnings and personalized recommendations.

price.note: Core tracking is free; optional StoryGraph Plus adds paid features such as roadmap voting and priority support.

products.name: Goodreads
products.description: The largest mainstream book-recommendation and review network; useful for discovery, but Amazon-owned and data-advertising aligned.

ethics.note: Goodreads is owned by Amazon, so it is a weak choice for readers trying to avoid Amazon-controlled book discovery.

local.note: Goodreads discovery does not inherently support local bookstores, indie retailers or libraries.

openness.note: It is a reviews and recommendations platform, not an ownership path for DRM-free or portable ebooks.

selection.note: Goodreads describes itself as the world's largest site for readers and book recommendations.

price.note: Discovery and tracking are free, but Goodreads' privacy notice ties use to Amazon data practices and interest-based advertising.

products.name: GlobalComix
products.description: A comics and manga reading platform with publisher catalogs, creator uploads, subscriptions and some paid PDF downloads.

ethics.note: GlobalComix gives creators and publishers direct-to-consumer publishing and monetization tools, including stated revenue shares.

local.note: It can help independent comics creators reach readers, but it is an online platform rather than a local comic shop.

openness.note: Many reads are platform-based, though GlobalComix also supports paid PDF download sales where publishers enable them.

selection.note: GlobalComix presents a broad comics, graphic-novel and manga catalog including major publishers and independent creators.

price.note: The platform combines previews, subscription reading, donations and paid digital downloads, so affordability varies by title and plan.

products.name: izneo
products.description: A digital comics, manga and graphic-novel storefront and app, especially useful for European comics access.

ethics.note: izneo is an authorized digital comics store/app, but its consumer model is conventional platform retail rather than author-direct or community-owned.

local.note: It gives access to comics catalogs online, but does not support local comic shops or libraries by default.

openness.note: izneo is a 100% digital reading app/store, so access generally depends on the platform rather than portable owned files.

selection.note: The izneo app listing describes a catalog of several thousand manga, BD, graphic novels and comics across devices.

price.note: Readers can buy albums and use promotions or subscription-style access, but prices and availability vary by country and title.

products.name: MANGA Plus by SHUEISHA
products.description: Shueisha's official global manga reader for free latest chapters and paid app-based access to larger backlists.

ethics.note: MANGA Plus is an official Shueisha service, so it is a legitimate rightsholder route for supported manga instead of piracy.

local.note: It supports official publisher distribution, but it does not support local bookstores, libraries or independent comic shops.

openness.note: Reading is app/web-platform based, and free first-read or subscription access does not mean portable ownership.

selection.note: MANGA Plus focuses on Shueisha titles, with latest chapters and paid MAX plans for broader English-chapter access.

price.note: Latest chapters are available free in the official app, and MAX plans add paid access to larger chapter catalogs.

products.name: OpenEdition Books
products.description: An open-access academic books platform for humanities and social-science titles, especially from European scholarly presses.

ethics.note: OpenEdition is a scholarly electronic-resources portal for humanities and social sciences, including OpenEdition Books.

local.note: It supports university and scholarly-press publishing, but is not a local bookstore or public-library route.

openness.note: OpenEdition foregrounds open access and web reading, with some downloadable formats tied to institutional services.

selection.note: OpenEdition Books is one of OpenEdition's four platforms and hosts a continuing catalog of scholarly books.

price.note: Web access to open texts is free, while some detached formats such as PDF or ePub can depend on institutional subscription services.

products.name: Standard Ebooks
products.description: A volunteer-produced catalog of free, DRM-free public-domain ebooks with strong formatting, accessibility and metadata standards.

ethics.note: Standard Ebooks produces free public-domain editions and uses an open volunteer production model rather than retail lock-in.

local.note: It is a global online commons project, not a local bookstore or library branch.

openness.note: Its ebooks are free of cost, free of U.S. copyright restrictions and distributed in portable ebook formats without retailer DRM.

selection.note: The catalog is intentionally curated and production-quality, so coverage is far narrower than mass ebook stores or large archives.

price.note: All produced ebooks are distributed free of cost.

products.name: Wikisource
products.description: A Wikimedia-hosted library of public-domain or freely redistributable source texts, useful for classics, historical documents and primary sources.

ethics.note: Wikisource is an official Wikimedia Foundation sister project built around free source texts rather than retailer sales.

local.note: It supports a global volunteer commons rather than local bookstores or library institutions.

openness.note: Wikisource describes its collection as public-domain or legally redistributable source texts.

selection.note: Coverage is broad for source texts and public-domain works, but uneven for recent commercial books.

price.note: The site is free to read online.

products.name: Wikibooks
products.description: A Wikimedia project for open-content textbooks, manuals, annotated texts and instructional guides.

ethics.note: Wikibooks is a Wikimedia commons project focused on developing open-content instructional books.

local.note: It is a global volunteer publishing project rather than a local bookstore or public-library service.

openness.note: The project is explicitly for open-content textbooks and instructional materials.

selection.note: Useful for some learning topics, but limited by volunteer coverage and not intended as a general ebook catalog.

price.note: Wikibooks content is free to read online.

products.name: Internet Archive Texts
products.description: A large nonprofit digital archive of free downloadable texts and borrowable modern ebooks, strongest for breadth and preservation.

ethics.note: Internet Archive is a nonprofit preservation route, though its controlled digital lending model has been legally contested by publishers.

local.note: It functions as a public digital archive, but does not support a user's local bookstore directly.

openness.note: The Texts collection includes freely downloadable books alongside borrowable modern ebooks, so openness varies by item.

selection.note: The Texts landing page reports more than 20 million freely downloadable books and texts plus a large borrowable ebook collection.

price.note: Reading and borrowing routes are generally free, though availability and formats vary by item.

products.name: NLS BARD
products.description: The U.S. National Library Service download platform for eligible patrons to access audio books, magazines, music materials and electronic braille.

ethics.note: BARD is a public accessible-reading service run through the Library of Congress NLS network for readers with qualifying print disabilities.

local.note: Enrollment flows through NLS network libraries that serve a patron's state or locality.

openness.note: Access is free but restricted to eligible NLS patrons, so it is not an open public ebook catalog.

selection.note: NLS says BARD provides instant access to hundreds of thousands of books, magazines and music materials.

price.note: BARD Mobile is free to download, and enrolled patrons use the service without retail purchase.

products.name: Library of Congress Digital Collections
products.description: A large U.S. public-library archive of digitized books, printed material and special collections, especially strong for historical and primary-source reading.

ethics.note: The Library of Congress is a public institution providing online digital collections rather than a retail bookstore.

local.note: It is a national public institution; it supports public access but not a user's local bookstore ecosystem.

openness.note: Many books and printed materials are available online with page views, text, image or PDF options, though rights and formats vary by item.

selection.note: The online Books/Printed Material search showed hundreds of thousands of available-online records, but it is strongest for archives and public-domain materials rather than current trade books.

price.note: Online digital collection access is free.

products.name: National Academies Press
products.description: A nonprofit scholarly press for National Academies reports and proceedings, with many titles available to read online or download as free PDFs.

ethics.note: The National Academies are private nonprofit institutions publishing evidence-based reports, proceedings and expert material through NAP.

local.note: NAP supports nonprofit scholarly publishing, but it is not a local bookstore or public-library route.

openness.note: NAP offers many publications for online reading and free PDF download, with ebook formats for thousands of titles.

selection.note: Selection is strong for science, engineering, medicine and policy reports, but narrow for general-interest fiction or trade books.

price.note: Many NAP titles can be read online or downloaded as free PDFs, while some formats or print editions may cost money.

products.name: Faded Page
products.description: A volunteer-run ebook project making works that are public domain in Canada freely available, often complementing U.S.-centric public-domain catalogs.

ethics.note: Faded Page says it is volunteer-run and works with Distributed Proofreaders Canada to make public-domain-in-Canada ebooks freely available.

local.note: It supports a volunteer commons, but is not a local bookstore or library service for most readers.

openness.note: The project makes ebooks freely available without cost, with the important caveat that public-domain status can differ outside Canada.

selection.note: The catalog is useful but modest compared with larger public-domain repositories.

price.note: Faded Page describes its mission as making ebooks available freely and without cost.

products.name: Open Book Publishers
products.description: A scholar-led, not-for-profit open-access academic press with free online reading and downloads across disciplines.

ethics.note: Open Book Publishers describes itself as award-winning, not-for-profit, run by scholars, and committed to free worldwide access.

local.note: It supports a scholar-led publishing commons rather than a local bookstore or public-library branch.

openness.note: The press says readers can access all books online or download them for free, with no mandatory author fees.

selection.note: Open Book Publishers reports over 450 titles, strong for academic monographs but narrow compared with a general bookstore.

price.note: Reader-facing access is free online or by download; print editions and optional support cost money.

products.name: MIT Press Open Access Books
products.description: MIT Press's open-access book program, useful for scholarly books in technology, design, science, society, and the arts.

ethics.note: MIT Press describes itself as a leading university press and says it has pushed open-access book publishing for close to 30 years.

local.note: This supports university-press scholarly publishing, but it is not a local bookstore or neighborhood library route.

openness.note: MIT Press says its open-access program includes more than 350 open-access books and a Direct to Open model.

selection.note: Selection is meaningful for MIT Press subject areas, but limited to one publisher's catalog.

price.note: Open-access titles are reader-free online, while print or non-OA MIT Press books may still cost money.

products.name: Project MUSE Open Access
products.description: A library-trusted platform hosting open-access books, journals, and digital humanities work from scholarly publishers.

ethics.note: Project MUSE says its OA content comes from university presses, scholarly societies, and independent not-for-profit academic publishers.

local.note: MUSE is library infrastructure rather than a local shop, and its OA metadata is designed for library discovery systems.

openness.note: Project MUSE states OA content requires no login, is DRM-free, and allows unlimited downloading and printing.

selection.note: The platform offers thousands of OA books and journal articles, strongest for academic teaching and research.

price.note: Open-access material is freely available to libraries and users around the world without a subscription requirement.

products.name: UC Press Luminos
products.description: University of California Press's open-access monograph program, strongest for peer-reviewed humanities and social-science books.

ethics.note: Luminos uses UC Press's selection, peer review, production, and marketing standards for open-access monographs.

local.note: It supports university-press scholarly publishing and library partnership, not a local retail route.

openness.note: Luminos is UC Press's open-access publishing program for monographs.

selection.note: The catalog is curated and relatively focused compared with broad open-access aggregators.

price.note: The core reader value is free access to open monographs; print editions or other UC Press titles may cost money.

products.name: punctum books
products.description: An independent open-access publisher for experimental, critical, and humanities-oriented scholarly books.

ethics.note: punctum describes itself as an independent open-access publisher committed to sharing work with the global commons.

local.note: It supports independent scholar-led publishing, but it is not a local bookstore or public-library lending channel.

openness.note: The press foregrounds open access and global commons sharing as part of its publishing identity.

selection.note: The catalog is intentionally specialized, strongest for para-humanities and experimental scholarly work.

price.note: Open-access reading is free; readers may still buy print copies or support the press.

products.name: Open Humanities Press
products.description: A scholar-led humanities open-access press with book series in critical theory, media, culture, climate, and related fields.

ethics.note: Open Humanities Press frames open access as peer-reviewed scholarly materials made freely available, not unrefereed self-publication.

local.note: It supports a humanities publishing commons, though it is not a local bookstore or municipal library.

openness.note: OHP says open-access publications can be read and downloaded for free from any computer, anywhere in the world.

selection.note: OHP books are published through named series, making the catalog useful but specialized.

price.note: The open-access reading path is free; the tradeoff is a narrower scholarly catalog.

products.name: De Gruyter Brill Open Access Books
products.description: A large scholarly publisher's open-access book catalog, useful as a breadth route but less community-owned than nonprofit OA presses.

ethics.note: De Gruyter Brill frames open access as widening scholarly access, but it remains a commercial scholarly publisher using several OA funding models.

local.note: This is a global commercial publishing route, not local retail, public-library lending, or community-owned publishing.

openness.note: The publisher reports thousands of open-access books, alongside journals and institutional agreements.

selection.note: De Gruyter Brill reports more than 5,300 open-access books, making selection broad for scholarly material.

price.note: Reader access to open-access books is free, though author/institution-side funding models vary.

products.name: Open Book Collective
products.description: A charity-owned platform for discovering and supporting open-access book publishers and infrastructure, especially relevant for libraries and institutions.

ethics.note: Open Book Collective describes itself as a charity bringing together publishers, service providers, and scholarly libraries for sustainable OA books.

local.note: Its model directly supports scholarly libraries and smaller open-access publishers rather than commercial platform consolidation.

openness.note: The platform helps readers and authors search and access open-access content from OBC publishers.

selection.note: It is a curated collective and catalog, useful for discovery but not as broad as a general book marketplace or open-access aggregator.

price.note: Reader discovery is free, but its institutional support model involves paid library subscriptions and packages.

products.name: Open Culture Free eBooks
products.description: A curated free-ebook list pointing readers toward public-domain and freely available books across classics, nonfiction, and poetry.

ethics.note: Open Culture is a discovery site for free educational media; it points outward rather than operating as a publisher or library.

local.note: It is a web discovery route rather than a local bookstore, library, or author-support channel.

openness.note: The ebook page links to downloadable or online free works, often via Project Gutenberg, Wikisource, Archive, or other hosts.

selection.note: Open Culture lists about 800 free ebooks, useful for classics discovery but small compared with full libraries.

price.note: The reader-facing list is explicitly for free ebooks.

products.name: ManyBooks
products.description: A large free-ebook and discounted-ebook discovery site, useful for price but less institutionally strong than libraries or nonprofit public-domain projects.

ethics.note: ManyBooks offers free ebooks and discounted bestseller promotion, but it is a commercial-style discovery site rather than a library or author-first platform.

local.note: It does not support local bookstores or public libraries directly.

openness.note: ManyBooks emphasizes free ebooks, but file rights, formats, and terms vary by title and source.

selection.note: The site says it has more than 50,000 free ebooks waiting to be discovered.

price.note: ManyBooks highlights a large free catalog plus discounted ebooks; not everything promoted is free.

products.name: Kindle Unlimited
products.description: Amazon's ebook subscription route: very broad and convenient for heavy Kindle readers, but access disappears when the subscription ends.

ethics.note: KDP Select authors are paid from a Kindle Unlimited global fund based on pages read, which rewards reading but keeps authors inside Amazon's program.

local.note: Kindle Unlimited is an Amazon subscription platform, not a local bookstore, library, or independent retail route.

openness.note: Amazon says cancelled members lose access to their Kindle Unlimited titles after the membership period ends.

selection.note: Amazon says Kindle Unlimited offers more than 5 million digital books, audiobooks, comics, and magazines, with up to 20 borrowed at a time.

price.note: Amazon lists the US membership at $11.99/month plus taxes, which can be economical for heavy readers but is a subscription rather than ownership.

products.name: Spotify Audiobooks
products.description: A convenient audiobook add-on for people already inside Spotify, strongest on convenience and catalog discovery rather than ownership.

ethics.note: Spotify for Authors provides publisher and self-published author tools, but audiobook economics still run through a large centralized platform.

local.note: Spotify is a global platform route and does not support local bookstores or public libraries directly.

openness.note: Spotify's support docs say Premium audiobook hours expire monthly and unused hours do not roll over.

selection.note: Spotify advertises a subscriber audiobook catalog of more than 700,000 titles.

price.note: Selected Premium plans include monthly audiobook listening time, while add-ons and the Audiobooks Access plan add extra paid routes.

products.name: Perlego
products.description: A textbook subscription that can reduce sticker shock for students and researchers, but it is still subscription access rather than open ownership.

ethics.note: Perlego describes its mission as making knowledge more accessible while working with educators and publishers.

local.note: Perlego is a centralized subscription platform rather than a local bookstore, library, or campus-owned OER collection.

openness.note: Perlego pricing describes plans that provide access to a level of library content and features, not unrestricted file ownership.

selection.note: Perlego advertises more than 1.5 million academic and professional ebooks from thousands of publishers.

price.note: The service positions itself as affordable course-material access through monthly, semester, or annual subscription plans.

products.name: LibreTexts Bookshelves
products.description: A nonprofit open-education platform with remixable textbook libraries, especially useful when a course can use or adapt open materials.

ethics.note: LibreTexts describes itself as a nonprofit open-education platform for creating, customizing, and sharing accessible interactive textbooks.

local.note: LibreTexts supports institutional publishing and campus/custom remixing rather than a purely commercial retail platform.

openness.note: LibreTexts Bookshelves are curated texts that can be used directly or remixed into customized course materials.

selection.note: LibreTexts reports thousands of textbooks and millions of pages of OER content across subject libraries.

price.note: LibreTexts is an open educational resource route, so reader access to the textbook materials is free.

products.name: B.C. Open Collection
products.description: A public open-education collection for finding free, open, customizable course materials, strongest for educators and students in common subjects.

ethics.note: BCcampus Open Collection is a publicly supported open-education route for educators and course materials.

local.note: The collection is rooted in British Columbia public education while remaining useful as an open resource beyond B.C.

openness.note: The collection presents free, open, and customizable materials by course or subject.

selection.note: The catalog includes open course materials across many subjects, with visible subject counts for business, sciences, math, humanities, trades, and more.

price.note: The collection is explicitly for free open course materials, making reader cost the main strength.
